gaps.text: In-line measurement of Cell density / turbidity with optical density / turbidity sensor
In-line measurement of Temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion of synchronised Raman and NIR spectra into one augmented matrix, as in the published pharma example. Both probes must sample the same well-mixed spot and the data must be normalised to a common time step, with block scaling so neither method dominates. Each method keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs or it is dropped.)
Achievable in situ accuracy for glucose and lactate in this customer's medium

items.finding: The temperature sensitivity of the OH bands presents a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR.
items.how_it_applies: The assessment should consider whether temperature fluctuations in the culture medium could interfere with NIR measurements, potentially requiring strict temperature control or compensation.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This finding addresses aqueous solutions in general rather than this specific cell culture matrix or instrument setup.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges data into a new matrix where variables from different sources are placed one after the other.
items.how_it_applies: This approach can be tested to combine Raman and NIR spectral data for the cell culture monitoring pilot, provided the data streams are properly aligned.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited review discusses general analytical techniques rather than the specific combination of Raman and NIR in a cell culture bioreactor.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31
